questions.q: Which country lies along Lombardy's northern border, just above the Valtellina?
questions.exp: Lombardy runs north to the Swiss border, as the Court's location cell says, with the Valtellina lying just below it; Austria borders Trentino-Alto Adige, France borders Piedmont and Valle d'Aosta, and Slovenia borders Friuli.

questions.q: Which region runs from the Po plain south east to the Adriatic at Rimini, straddling northern and central Italy?
questions.exp: Emilia-Romagna stretches across the peninsula from the Po to the Adriatic, Emilia in the west around Modena and Reggio, Romagna in the east, and the Court places it astride the north and the centre; the Marche lies south of it, while Lombardy and Friuli-Venezia Giulia are wholly northern.

questions.q: Which climate category does the Court give Lombardy and Emilia-Romagna?
questions.exp: The Court files both regions as cool continental: cold winters and warm summers with no sea to soften them, tempered in Lombardy by its lakes and on the Emilian hills by altitude. Neither is Mediterranean or maritime in the Court's terms.

questions.q: Franciacorta's vines grow in the province of Brescia, on low hills at the southern end of a lake that tempers the climate. Name the lake.
questions.exp: Lake Iseo, between Bergamo and Brescia, moderates winter cold and summer heat over Franciacorta; it is one of the many lakes the Court says influence Lombardy, with Garda to the east and Como to the west.

questions.q: By which method does the Court say most Lambrusco is made sparkling?
questions.exp: Most Lambrusco is made frizzante or spumante in pressurised tanks by cuve close, the Charmat method, which keeps its fruit bright. The Court adds that some is made by metodo classico or the méthode ancestrale; the transfer method is no Lambrusco technique.

questions.q: Counting from the harvest, how many months must pass before a non vintage Franciacorta may be released?
questions.exp: A non vintage Franciacorta must spend at least 18 months on its lees and may not be released until 25 months after the harvest, the two figures the Court prints; a Millesimato needs 30 months on the lees and a Riserva 60.

questions.q: What is the highest pressure a Franciacorta Satèn may hold in the bottle?
questions.exp: Satèn may hold at most 5 atmospheres, against about 6 for most Franciacorta, which gives its softer, creamier mousse; the Court adds that it is Brut only and made from white grapes, Chardonnay with up to half Pinot Bianco.

questions.q: Chardonnay leads a Franciacorta Satèn. Which grape may make up as much as half of the blend beside it?
questions.exp: Satèn is a white grape Franciacorta, Chardonnay with up to 50 per cent Pinot Bianco as the Court's cell says, so Pinot Nero, which may go into the other Franciacorta styles, is shut out of it.

questions.q: Which word on a Lambrusco label marks the sweetest of the three levels the Court names?
questions.exp: Lambrusco is labelled Secco when dry, Amabile when medium sweet and Dolce when sweet, the Court's three sweetness words; Abboccato, a step between Secco and Amabile, also turns up on some labels.

questions.q: Bellavista is one of the two Franciacorta houses the Court names. Which of these is the other?
questions.exp: Ca' del Bosco and Bellavista, both at Erbusco, are the Court's two Franciacorta producers; Ferrari makes Trento DOC, Contratto is a Canelli house for Piedmontese metodo classico, and Villa Sandi is a Prosecco producer.

questions.q: A bar pours Lambrusco by the glass. Which quality of an opened bottle fades first and limits how long it can be sold?
questions.exp: The Court's business cell warns that Lambrusco's gentle frizzante sparkle has a short life once the bottle is open, so a by the glass programme should open bottles to demand, close them with a sparkling stopper and cost in the waste.

questions.q: How does the Court say a Lambrusco should be served to a guest?
opts: Cold, in a flute or a wine glass
At cellar temperature, in a large bowl
At room temperature, in a tumbler
Lightly chilled, in a coupe only
questions.exp: Lambrusco is served as any other sparkling wine, cold and in a flute or a wine glass, the Court's own service cell, which also points to its published sparkling wine service standards; served warm, its fruit and froth soon tire.
